newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Trans-World not controlling Russian aluminium - Kokh.
newsitem.headline: Trans-World not controlling Russian aluminium - Kokh.

text.p: British commodities powerhouse Trans-World Group does not control Russia's aluminium industry, and there is no legal basis for believing the group is linked to illegal activity, Russian privatisation minister said Thursday.
"There is a stereotypical view that bandits control aluminium companies (in Russia)," Deputy Prime Minister Alfred Kokh told a news conference.
"I can say that that is not so. Even completely not so," he said, adding there was no legal basis to believe that Transworld through subsidiaries was illegally involved in the industry.
Kokh said Trans-World's control was limited to the Bratsk and Sayansk aluminium groups, Russia's first and third largest aluminium producers respectively.
"They do not even control half the production...it is already clear Trans-World does not control the industry," he said.
"(Also) they have practically no control over alumina production," he said of Trans-World.

Trans-World, a major trading company, has invested millions of dollars in the Russian metals industry, and uses Russian plants to produce refined metal under tolling operations, whereby Russian smelters process alumina imported by the group.
Trans-World is at the centre of a bitter row with Moscow over how much control foreign companies should have over the lucrative Russian aluminium business.
The spat has raised questions over whether Russian supplies of primary aluminium to world markets might be jeopardised.
Russian is the world's biggest aluminium exporter, delivering 2.44 million tonnes to markets last year out of total production of 2.87 million.
Kokh named a list of major aluminium producers, including Krasnoyarsk Aluminium, Russia's second largest producer as those not under Trans-World control.

Trans-World alleged in 1994 that Krasnoyarsk had expunged a major stake it had in the plant from the shareholder registery. The company is fighting in Moscow's federal court to have the stake in the smelter re-listed.
